content.text: -    MOA: central α2 adrenergic agonist -> ↓sympathetic outflow
-    Clin Use: also smoke cessation (2nd-line, if 1st-line fails)
-    Caution: rebound HTN if abrupt d/c (taper slowly)
-    MOA: central α2A agonist -> ↑postsynaptic prefrontal cortex signaling -> ↑attention/↓impulsivity (⍉ CNS stimulant)
-    Caution: rebound HTN if abrupt d/c    -    taper slowly
: (1) stim alpha-2A receptors on presynaptic neurons in the CNS to
, (2) also work @ postsynaptic receptors to increase blood flow in the prefrontal cortex, which has been shown to enhance working memory and executive functioning
: ADHD in children ≥6yo; ⍉indication for ADHD in adults
•may be used as monotx or as adjunct therapy to stimulants to reduce disruptive behavior, control aggression, or improve sleep in youth (sedation effect)
•dose-dependent CV events (brady, hypotension, orthostasis, syncope), sedation, & drowsiness
•abrupt D/C can cause rebound HTN, nervousness, anxiety
•Guanfacine: skin rash (rare, but serious; D/C if occurs)

content.text: -    Monitoring: baseline EKG w ped (♡ RF/Fx)    -    HR/BP    -    d/c if new CV sx
-    Admin: ↑dose wkly    -    immediate    -    IR/ER (both = same med)
-    SE:           insomnia (d/c PM dose)                      -    ↓wt: dose post-↑cal meal
tic (↓dose OR alt OR α2-agonist)     -    growth delay (drug holiday)
-    Pt ed: monitor growth/wt     -    abuse potential (C-2)    -    ⍉PM dose

content.text: Ritalin, Ritalin SR, Methylin, Metadate ER or CD, Concerta, Daytrana- patch
abrupt d/c -> w.draw sx - taper after chronic use
taper if long ↑dose use - fatigue, depression
+5 mg q wk; +2.5 mg q wk
SWD: 150 mg ~1 h b4 work shift
peds <70 kg: 0.5 mg/kg/day; peds ±70 kg/adults: 40 mg/day
: block presynaptic DA and NE reuptake; amphetamines also increase DA release; inhibit MAO
•psychiatric – psychosis, mood disturb, severe anxiety or panic attacks
•⍉in pts w/ known ♡ abnormalities ← ↑risk of sudden death – specifically, some agents are CI in pts w/ HF, recent MI, arrhythmia, or mod-severe HTN
•most stimulants are CI in pts w/ marked anxiety, tension, agitation, glaucoma, hyperthyroidism, or hx of a tic dx
: CNS stimulants, incl amphetamine ER oral formulations, other amphetamine-containing prod, and methylphenidate, have a ↑potential for abuse and dependence
: misuse may cause sudden death & serious CV events
: severe CV events & other vasc problems, increase suicidality, exacerbate pre-existing psychiatric disorders, seizures, stunted growth, serotonin syndrome

content.text: Methylphenidate (Ritalin, Ritalin SR, Methylin, Metadate ER or CD, Concerta, Daytrana- patch)
-    MOA: block DAT/NET -> ⍉ DA/NE reuptake -> ↑[DA/NE synaptic] (⍉ direct release — needs neuron firing; unlike amphetamine)
-    SE: priapism (urgent)    -    periph vasculopathy/Raynaud    -    fever    -    sz
-     Pt ed: swallow Concerta whole -⍉ split/crush/chew
severe depression on w.draw    -    Hx substance abuse/alcoholism
Dexmethylphenidate (Focalin, Focalin XR): d-threo enantiomer of racemic methylphenidate

pieces.file: Behavioral Health Med List and LOs (6)

content.text: -    MOA: DAT/NET substrate -> into neuron -> displaces vesicular NT (VMAT2) -> MAO-i (⍉ met) -> reverses DAT/NET -> efflux to synapse -> ↑↑[DA/NE synaptic] (weak 5HT)
-    Clin Use: ↑alert/insomnia    -    ↓fatigue/appetite    -    3:1 d:l amphetamine salts    -    Tmax ~7 h (XR)
-    SE: C-2    -    CNS (weakness, dizziness, confusion, delirium, SI)    -    CV (arrhythmias, angina pain)    -    diarrhea
-    CI: HTN/CVD/AS    -    hyperthyroidism    -    Hx drug abuse    -    MAOI w.in 14D
-    BBW: C-2    -    drug dep    -    sudden death    -    serious ♡ effects
: enter the sympathetic n. ending and displace stored catecholamine transmitter

content.text: -    MOA: selective NE reuptake-i (NRI) -> ↑NE synaptic (⍉ direct DA release    -    ⍉ controlled/⍉ abuse)
-    Caution: hepatotox (rare — d/c if jaundice/↑LFTs)    -    ↑BP/HR    -    4-6 wk onset
-    BBW: ↑SI (peds/adolesc — monitor esp early tx & dose chg)
: may inhibit the reuptake of released transmitter by interfering w the action of the NE transporter, NET
: approved for use in adults & children ≥6yo; second line
•less potential for growth suppression but greater risk of fatigue, sedation, & dizziness
: glaucoma, pheochromocytoma, severe CVD, MAOI use w.in 14d
: psychiatric (aggression, psychotic sxs), orthostasis, syncope, allergic rxns, priapism, hepatotoxicity, serious CV events, growth issues
